ahasuerus-esther.name: Ahasuerus, the king in Esther
ahasuerus-esther.role: Persian king whose orders shape the crisis
ahasuerus-esther.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahasuerus-esther.importance: His choices spread danger and later give the Jews power to fight their enemies.
ahasuerus-esther.connections: He removes Vashti, makes Esther queen, and gives his ring to Haman and Mordecai.

vashti.name: Vashti
vashti.role: Queen removed after refusing the king’s order
vashti.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
vashti.importance: Her refusal leads the king’s advisers to demand rules for all wives.
vashti.connections: She holds a feast for women. She refuses to appear when the king sends servants.

memucan.name: Memucan
memucan.role: Adviser who urges the king to replace Vashti
memucan.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
memucan.importance: He turns the king’s anger into a claim that all husbands need protection.
memucan.connections: He is one of seven princes close to the king.

royal-servants-esther.name: The seven royal servants
royal-servants-esther.role: Servants sent to bring Vashti before the king
royal-servants-esther.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
royal-servants-esther.importance: They carry the order that Vashti refuses.
royal-servants-esther.connections: The list names Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcass.

royal-princes-esther.name: The king’s princes
royal-princes-esther.role: Advisers who know the laws and meet the king
royal-princes-esther.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
royal-princes-esther.importance: The king asks these advisers how to answer Vashti’s refusal.
royal-princes-esther.connections: Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, and Marsena sit with Memucan.

esther.name: Esther
esther.role: Jewish queen who asks the king to save her people
esther.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
esther.importance: She risks approaching the king and keeps asking for help after Haman dies.
esther.connections: Also called Hadassah, she is Abihail’s daughter. Mordecai raises her after her parents die.

mordecai.name: Mordecai
mordecai.role: Esther’s cousin and guardian, later a high official
mordecai.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
mordecai.importance: His messages urge Esther to act. His later letters help organize defense and yearly remembrance.
mordecai.connections: He raises Esther, reports a plot against the king, and refuses to bow to Haman.

hegai.name: Hegai
hegai.role: Royal servant in charge of the first women’s house
hegai.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hegai.importance: His care helps Esther within a household controlled by the king.
hegai.connections: He gives Esther food, cosmetics, attendants, and advice before she meets the king.

shaashgaz.name: Shaashgaz
shaashgaz.role: Royal servant keeping the second women’s house
shaashgaz.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shaashgaz.importance: His task shows how the king controls whether women return to see him.
shaashgaz.connections: Women enter his care after spending a night with the king.

abihail-esther.name: Abihail, Esther’s father
abihail-esther.role: Mordecai’s uncle and Esther’s deceased father
abihail-esther.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abihail-esther.importance: Naming her father connects the queen to the family she first keeps secret.
abihail-esther.connections: Mordecai takes Esther into his family after both her parents die.

mordecai-ancestors.name: Jair, Shimei, and Kish in Mordecai’s family
mordecai-ancestors.role: Three ancestors named before the exile account
mordecai-ancestors.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
mordecai-ancestors.importance: Their names connect Mordecai’s family with the earlier loss of Jerusalem.
mordecai-ancestors.connections: The list calls Mordecai a son of Jair, Shimei, and Kish, from Benjamin’s family.

bigthan-teresh.name: Bigthan and Teresh
bigthan-teresh.role: Two doorkeepers who plot against the king
bigthan-teresh.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
bigthan-teresh.importance: The saved report later prompts the king to reward Mordecai. Chapter six calls Bigthan Bigthana.
bigthan-teresh.connections: Mordecai reports their plot through Esther. The king’s investigation leads to their deaths.

esther-maidens.name: Esther’s attendants
esther-maidens.role: Women serving Esther in the palace
esther-maidens.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
esther-maidens.importance: Esther prepares with others before facing the danger of approaching the king.
esther-maidens.connections: Hegai gives her seven attendants. Later, her women join her three-day fast.

haman.name: Haman
haman.role: Official who plans to kill all the Jews
haman.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
haman.importance: He uses the king’s authority against a whole people after Mordecai refuses to bow.
haman.connections: Hammedatha’s son, called an Agagite, receives high office. His wife is Zeresh.

zeresh.name: Zeresh
zeresh.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zeresh.importance: Her advice changes as Haman’s apparent success becomes public humiliation.
zeresh.connections: She joins his friends in proposing a gallows. Later, she warns that he will fall.

hathach.name: Hathach
hathach.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hathach.importance: His messages let Esther learn about the death order and answer Mordecai’s request.
hathach.connections: The king assigns him to Esther. He visits Mordecai outside the gate.

harbonah.name: Harbonah
harbonah.role: Royal servant who points out Haman’s gallows
harbonah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
harbonah.importance: His words connect Haman’s death plan with Mordecai’s earlier service to the king.
harbonah.connections: He speaks to the king after Esther names Haman as her enemy.

jewish-families-esther.name: The Jewish families in Esther
jewish-families-esther.role: Men, women, and children threatened by Haman’s letters
jewish-families-esther.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jewish-families-esther.importance: The danger reaches whole families. Remembrance includes food gifts and help for people in need.
jewish-families-esther.connections: They mourn and fast, then gather to fight. Later, they keep Purim each year.

royal-scribes-esther.name: The royal writers
royal-scribes-esther.role: Writers preparing orders in many languages
royal-scribes-esther.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
royal-scribes-esther.importance: Written words carry the king’s power far beyond his palace.
royal-scribes-esther.connections: They write Haman’s orders and later write what Mordecai commands.

royal-couriers-esther.name: The royal couriers
royal-couriers-esther.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
royal-couriers-esther.importance: The letters reach distant communities before the chosen day of fighting.
royal-couriers-esther.connections: They hurry out with the first death order. Later, riders carry the new letters.

haman-sons.name: Haman’s ten sons
haman-sons.role: Family members killed during the fighting in Susa
haman-sons.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
haman-sons.importance: Their deaths extend the conflict beyond Haman himself. The account gives none of their own words.
haman-sons.connections: They are killed before Esther asks the king to hang their bodies.

jehoiachin.name: Jehoiachin
jehoiachin.role: Judah’s king named in the earlier exile account
jehoiachin.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jehoiachin.importance: His name connects the Persian setting with an earlier loss of Judah’s freedom.
jehoiachin.connections: Esther’s family account names him among those carried away by Nebuchadnezzar.

nebuchadnezzar.name: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar.role: Earlier Babylonian king named in Esther’s family account
nebuchadnezzar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nebuchadnezzar.importance: His earlier conquests form part of the family’s remembered past.
nebuchadnezzar.connections: The account recalls his capture of people from Jerusalem.
